title: Negative diffusivity of excitons in electron-hole plasmas
abstract: We develop a minimal hydrodynamic framework to describe exciton transport in the presence of an electron hole plasma in 2D semiconductors. Treating excitons, electrons, and holes as coupled fluids, we show that exciton diffusion is strongly renormalized by momentum exchange with the plasma. In the collisional regime, mutual diffusion leads to a nontrivial redistribution of transport coefficients but preserves the positivity of the exciton diffusivity. In contrast, when plasma inertia and collective charge oscillations are accounted for, the exciton diffusive mode hybridizes with acoustic plasma modes, giving rise to a dynamical instability manifested as an effective negative diffusion coefficient. We demonstrate that this instability originates from the nonequilibrium coupling between slow excitons and fast plasma degrees of freedom, rather than from nonlinear diffusion or thermodynamic effects. Our results provide a unified physical mechanism for negative exciton diffusivity reported in recent experiments and establish collective plasma dynamics as a key control parameter of exciton transport in 2D materials.
summary: This paper develops a hydrodynamic model for exciton transport coupled to an electron-hole plasma in 2D semiconductors. It shows that while simple collision models predict positive diffusion, including the inertia of the plasma leads to hybridization with acoustic plasmon modes. This coupling generates a dynamical instability, manifesting as a theoretically predicted negative effective exciton diffusivity.
main_problem: The study investigates exciton transport dynamics, specifically focusing on the theoretical conditions under which an effective negative diffusion coefficient can arise in two-dimensional semiconductors.
main_result: Negative exciton diffusivity is predicted to occur when the system's collective plasma oscillations (plasmons) couple strongly with the slow excitonic motion, leading to a dynamical instability rather than simple nonlinear effects.
method: The authors developed and utilized a minimal hydrodynamic framework by treating excitons, electrons, and holes as coupled fluids, analyzing the resulting dispersion relations in Fourier space.
model_or_system: The physical system is an exciton-electron-hole plasma within 2D semiconductors (like TMDs). The model treats the three species using coupled fluid dynamics equations, moving from simple collision models to full self-consistent analysis incorporating plasmons.
key_observables: Effective exciton diffusivity ($D_{eff}^X$), dispersion relation ($\omega$), and the sign of the effective diffusion coefficient (positive for damping, negative for instability).
important_parameters: Plasma inertia, collective charge oscillation frequency ($\omega_p$), collision rates ($\gamma_X, \gamma_p$), and the degree of coupling between excitons and plasma modes.
main_assumptions: Initial analyses assume quasi-neutrality or symmetric effective masses; the key result requires incorporating plasmons beyond simple diffusive plasma dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates normal, dissipative diffusion (positive $D_{eff}^X$), while Figure 3 demonstrates the negative diffusion regime characterized by localized density enhancement and growing amplitude due to hybridization with the acoustic plasma mode.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing simple collisional regimes where diffusivity remains positive, through incorporating full self-consistent dynamics involving plasmons, culminating in the derivation of the instability condition leading to negative effective diffusivity.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the mechanism—where collective plasma modes drive a non-dissipative instability that modifies particle transport coefficients—is analogous to instabilities studied in open quantum systems or driven many-body dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Dispersion relation of the exciton-plasma system, in units of k0 = e2n0/(2meDX) and ω0 = DXk2 0. Top panel: normal modes in the absence of exciton-plasma coupling, γe = γh = 0, featuring a diffusive mode (ω1, red line), plasma acoustic (ω2, light blue line) and plasma optical (ω3, dark blue line). Right panel: the same modes as obtained for γe = γh = 0.1γX, and ¯vX = 2.8vth. In all the cases, we have assumed a diffusion constant of DX = 0.9v2 th/ωp.

FIG. 2. Diffusion dynamics in a quasi-one-dimensional channel. Normal diffusive transport, corresponding to eDX > 0, where the exciton density profile broadens in time and the peak amplitude decreases, in agreement with the purely dissipative regime described by Eq. (9).

FIG. 3. Diffusion dynamics in a quasi-one-dimensional channel. Negative diffusion regime, corresponding to eDX < 0, where the exciton density develops a localized enhancement and increases in amplitude, signaling a dynamical instability. This behavior originates from the hybridization between the exciton diffusive mode and the acoustic plasma mode, as described by Eq. (28), and provides a real-space manifestation of the gain predicted by the dispersion relation in Fig. 1.
